claims.hypothesis: Is the CO(3-2) emission of DLA-B1228g consistent with a rotation-dominated cold disk?
claims.experiment: qubefit MCMC fit of a thin exponential disk with constant v_rot and sigma_v to the 35 km/s ALMA cube
claims.result: v_rot = 328 +/- 7 km/s, sigma_v = 62 +/- 7 km/s, v_rot/sigma_v = 5.3 +/- 0.6, reduced chi-square 1.2, no significant residual
claims.finding: DLA-B1228g is a cold rotating disk, the second HI-absorption-selected galaxy so identified

evidence.quote: Kinematic modelling reveals that the CO(3–2) emission is consistent with arising from an axisymmetric rotating disk, with an exponential profile, a rotation velocity of $v_{rot}=328\pm7$ km s$^{-1}$, and a velocity dispersion of $\sigma_{v}=62\pm7$ km s$^{-1}$.

claims.hypothesis: Could the apparent disk kinematics instead arise from a major merger?
claims.experiment: Compare F160W morphology, Halpha, CO line profile symmetry, velocity dispersions in the two halves, and gas depletion time with merger expectations
claims.result: Clumpy F160W and kinematic-vs-physical centre offset favour a merger, but weak Halpha, symmetric double-peaked line, similar dispersions and ~1 Gyr depletion time disfavour it
claims.finding: A major merger is unlikely but cannot be formally ruled out with the present data

evidence.quote: It appears unlikely that the galaxy is a major merger system, although this scenario cannot be formally ruled out by the present data.

claims.experiment: Compare the CO-based dynamical mass within 2 R_e with the CO(1-0) molecular gas mass of Kaur et al. 2022a
claims.result: M_dyn = (1.5 +/- 0.1)e11 Msun versus M_mol ~ 1e11 Msun, with no stellar mass estimate

evidence.quote: We thus find that the central regions of DLA-B1228g are baryon-dominated, as has also been found for emission-selected galaxies at similar redshifts
We do not currently have an estimate of the stellar mass of DLA-B1228g.

claims.hypothesis: Does the damped Lyman-alpha absorption arise in an extended HI disk of the galaxy?
claims.experiment: Scale the local HI mass-size relation to an assumed HI mass of ~7.3e10 Msun, overlay the HI disk and expected velocity at the QSO sightline, compare to UVES Ni II absorption
claims.result: Sightline falls inside the expected HI disk (diameter >~160 kpc) but the metal absorption is redward of the expected -123 km/s
claims.finding: DLA absorption may arise in the HI disk, though a simple thin disk does not explain the metal-line velocities

evidence.loc: The z ≈ 2.1929 DLA: Disk or CGM?
evidence.quote: indicating that it is possible that the damped Lyman-$\alpha$ absorption arises in the Hi disk of the galaxy

evidence.loc: The z ≈ 2.1929 DLA: Disk or CGM?

claims.hypothesis: Is there a stellar counterpart to the CO emission?
claims.experiment: New HST WFC3 F160W image overlaid on CO(3-2) contours, plus F105W non-detection limit
claims.result: Extended F160W emission (~8 sigma) offset ~1.4-1.5 kpc from CO; F105W undetected to AB 26.5
claims.finding: The extended F160W emission is the stellar counterpart, and the galaxy is highly dust obscured

evidence.quote: This extended emission, at a rest-frame wavelength of $\approx 5000$ Å at $z \approx 2.193$, appears to be the stellar counterpart of the CO(3–2) emission.

why_this_data.value: DLA field previously detected in CO(3-2) at low resolution as part of a high-metallicity DLA sample; PKS B1228-113 chosen as pointing centre because it is bright at mm wavelengths and allows self-calibration

evidence.quote: This DLA field was originally searched for CO(3–2) emission by (cite: Neeleman18), as part of a sample of high-metallicity DLAs (cite: Kanekar20), and yielded a detection of strong CO(3–2) emission at low angular resolution
PKS B1228-113 was chosen as the pointing centre as it is bright at mm wavelengths, allowing self-calibration of the target field.

why_this_method.value: Simple axisymmetric exponential disk with constant v_rot and sigma_v because the CO S/N is modest and this model already fits

evidence.quote: In passing, we note that we used a simple axisymmetric exponential disk model, with a constant rotational velocity and velocity dispersion, for the kinematic modelling as the signal-to-noise ratio of the detected CO(3–2) emission is not very high.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cubes made at 25, 35, 50 km/s and robust -1 to +1; robust +1 at 35 km/s chosen for modelling (Table 1)

evidence.quote: using a range of velocity resolutions (25, 35, 50 km s$^{-1}$) and values of the robust parameter (-1, -0.5, 0, +0.5, +1)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Major-merger scenario considered and judged very unlikely

evidence.loc: Can the CO Kinematics be explained by a Major Merger?
evidence.quote: Overall, it appears very unlikely that DLA-B1228g is a major merger system

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: More complex kinematic models not tried since the simple model already fits

evidence.quote: Given that this model already provides a good fit, more complicated models (with more parameters) are also likely to yield good fits to the observed CO(3–2) emission.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Self-calibration stopped when no further improvement in image or residuals; final cube chosen on sensitivity/S/N versus resolution

evidence.quote: after which no further improvement was seen in either the image or the image/visibility residuals upon further self-calibration
based on a balance between the per-channel sensitivity and signal-to-noise ratio, and the angular resolution

limitations_admitted.value: Intermediate angular resolution and sensitivity, only 2-3 beams across the CO region, so a merger can mimic a disk

evidence.quote: we note that the current ALMA CO(3–2) image has intermediate angular resolution and sensitivity, with only $2-3$ synthesized beams across the CO-emitting region.

limitations_admitted.value: Dynamical mass error includes only the fit error; spherical assumption dominates the uncertainty

evidence.quote: We emphasize that the quoted error only includes the error from the fit.
We do not currently have an estimate of the stellar mass of DLA-B1228g.

referee_caveats_inferred: Constant v_rot and sigma_v with a thin disk and only 2-3 beams across the source: inclination, v_rot and sigma_v are degenerate and the quoted errors are likely underestimated.
qubefit priors, convergence and the meaning of '400,000 MCMC chains' are not given, so the stated uncertainties are hard to check.
The dynamical mass assumes sphericity and neglects sigma_v; the baryon-dominance claim relies on a CO(1-0) mass with an assumed alpha_CO and no stellar or HI mass.
The disk-versus-merger argument is qualitative; no merger model or comparison with simulations is fitted.
HI disk size of >~160 kpc is an extrapolation from the local mass-size relation with an assumed HI mass.
